sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Social Commerce via Short Video Platforms

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Napoleonic tradition; French Commercial Code, French Civil Code and French Monetary and Financial Code; unitary national jurisdiction with separate administrative- and commercial-court orders)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty of 30 May 1984 (in force)
France–People's Republic of China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement of 30 May 1984, as amended by the Additional Protocol of 26 November 2013
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI) signed 30 December 2020; ratification suspended, not yet in force
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applicable)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention of 19 June 2008
France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation of 31 August 1994, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (France), Book II, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 for Sociétés à Responsabilité Limitée; Articles L.123-1 to L.123-22 and R.123-101 to R.123-126 regarding the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS); Décret n°67-237 du 23 mars 1967 and the Guichet Unique implementing decrees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce of the registered office; filings submitted through the Guichet Unique operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (déclaration de création d'une société commerciale) accompanied by the executed statuts, capital deposit attestation, legal publication proof, and supporting exhibits.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to a French SARL; the capital is freely fixed in the statuts. Under Article L.223-7 of the Code de commerce, each cash contribution must be paid up to at least one-fifth at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. The funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account or with a notary and evidenced by an attestation de dépôt de fonds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE ASSOCIATES OF [FR_SARL]

At the constitutive meeting held on [date] at [address], the subscribers RESOLVED:

1. Share Subscription. The share capital of EUR [—], divided into [—] shares, is fully subscribed and paid up to the legally required minimum; the deposit certificate is annexed.

2. Registered Office. The office is fixed at [address], as legal seat for process and registration.

3. Appointment. [Name] is appointed Gérant, with full authority to bind the company, open bank accounts, employ staff, and sign tax and regulatory filings.

4. Registration. The Gérant is authorised to file the M0 form with the RCS, publish the formation notice, and complete all formalities.

This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital proofing and escrow deposit at a French bank or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank selected by the founders or a notary authorized to receive funds in escrow.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the future SARL and deposit the cash contributions declared in the draft statuts. The bank or notary must issue an attestation de dépôt des fonds confirming that the funds are blocked and will be released only upon registration in the RCS or under the statutory exceptions. Complete KYC, beneficial-owner identification, and source-of-funds documentation in parallel.
required_dossiers: Proof of residential address not older than three months
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC or source of funds, supply corrected proof of identity, address, and economic justification. If the bank refuses, select another EU-licensed credit institution or a notary and repeat the escrow deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution, signing of statuts and appointment of the first Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All founding associates and the proposed Gérant; a notary is required only if real property or certain in-kind contributions are made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize and sign the statuts. State the corporate name, registered office, corporate object, share capital, share distribution, governance rules, and the first Gérant. Obtain a written acceptance from the Gérant. If the registered office is not owned or leased by the company, obtain an office-occupancy agreement (convention d'occupation). Use certified electronic signatures if signing remotely and preserve the original signed PDF for the filing.
required_dossiers: Bank or notary capital deposit attestation
Office-occupancy agreement or ownership/title document for the registered office
Identity documents and residence proofs of all associates
Written acceptance of appointment by the first Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary identifies a substantive irregularity, execute a rectification deed or amend the statuts before filing. If signatures or shareholder coordinates are defective, re-sign a clean corrected page and annex it to the statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal notice in an authorized legal-announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorized in the département of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a concise constitution notice containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, identity of the Gérant, and the RCS court of registration. Submit the notice to the authorized newspaper and obtain the justificatif de parution, which must remain valid and be uploaded with the M0 filing.
required_dossiers: Final text of the constitution notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal-notice newspaper requests corrections, order a corrected publication or a rectifying notice and obtain a new justificatif de parution before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the M0 dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the official portal, choose creation of a commercial company, and complete the M0 declaration. Attach the signed statuts, capital deposit attestation, publication proof, office-occupancy proof, identity documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. Certify the declaration, pay the RCS/greffe fee online, and submit. INPI routes the dossier to the RCS, INSEE, tax, and social security authorities.
required_dossiers: Justificatif de parution of the legal notice
Office-occupancy agreement or title for the registered office
Identity documents of all managers and associates
Statutory declaration of non-conviction/incompatibility where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique issues an incompleteness notice, upload the missing item before the stated deadline. If the file is rejected, read the stated grounds, cure the deficient document, and resubmit promptly. For technical failures, contact INPI support or the assigned Greffe and preserve the ticket reference for restitution.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL entities obtain SIREN/SIRET via guichet-entreprises.fr or guichet-unique.fr; foreign entities register for VAT ID (FR + SIREN) on impots.gouv.fr upon exceeding turnover threshold or supplying taxable services in France
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; French SARL taxed at corporate level under impôt sur les sociétés. Limited regimes include micro-entreprise for small turnover or specific hybrid mismatch relief under EU directives

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Facture électronique de type 2 (FE2) for B2B transactions; real-time data exchange with DGFiP via API; digital tax stamps and clearance for cross-border supplies

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate on goods exported outside the EU and qualifying offshore services, requiring proof of export and non-EU destination
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Retrospective zero-rating if export not substantiated; penalties up to 80% of VAT due plus interest and possible criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank) acting with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision and the Direction Générale du Trésor / Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances for foreign exchange regulatory policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a euro-area member, operates full capital and current account convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements; no general exchange control restrictions apply to EUR transactions. Profit remittances by an SARL are freely permitted after corporate tax and legal reserve obligations, subject to standard anti-money laundering and beneficial-ownership verification by payment channels. Cross-border payments are generally unrestricted, but French resident entities must comply with monthly or quarterly balance-of-payments reporting to Banque de France where aggregate cross-border flows exceed EUR 50 million per annum; smaller flows are exempt from systematic granular reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists in France to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or to convert export receipts into EUR within a mandatory timeline. Exporters retain free disposition of foreign-currency proceeds. France has had no obligatory repatriation or conversion requirement since the full liberalisation of exchange controls; entities need only maintain supporting documentation for tax, customs, and balance-of-payments statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions licensed in the European Economic Area may legally operate in France under the EU payment services passport. Viability is Medium-High for ancillary payout and foreign-exchange services, such as Wise Business and specialised FX providers, but mainstream merchant treasury is still best concentrated in a licensed French commercial bank to secure merchant-of-record settlement flows, French VAT registration, and credible bank references. Legal constraints require the EMI to be registered with the ACPR or passported into France, funds to be safeguarded, client money to be segregated, and full KYC/KYB of the SARL to be performed before account opening.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in France is not an absolute legal requirement for bank account opening, but most tier-1 French commercial banks require an initial in-person meeting with the gérant (manager) and beneficial owners, or a notarised/consular attestation for remote signatures. Remote onboarding may be accepted for EU-established entities using qualified electronic signatures under eIDAS, but the practical stance of most French credit institutions remains strongly biased toward a physical interview at a branch or a bank officer visit. Non-resident managers without French identity documents should expect at least one physical visit to Paris or an acceptable video-identity procedure approved by the specific compliance department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: France-headquartered newly formed SARL with a sole non-resident manager and substantial anticipated TikTok Shop settlement velocity before full audited financial history exists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide original Kbis extract less than 3 months old, Articles of Association (statuts) with signed Gérant appointment, proof of registered office lease, valid passports of all beneficial owners and managers, personal and corporate proof of address, bank references from the shareholder entity, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, projected P&L and cash flow model, TikTok Shop seller agreements, marketplace statements and transaction history, VAT registration certificate, EORI number evidence, and a detailed beneficial ownership diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume non-face-to-face retail payment receipts, including rapid monthly turnover mismatch versus capital base and plausible third-party payout concentration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A contractual merchant-of-record or sub-merchant agreement with TikTok Shop / TikTok Pte Ltd, comprehensive platform payout reconciliation reports, invoices and shipping customs records (for goods in transit), carrier tracking evidence, supplier contracts with invoices, consolidated trade ledger with SKU-level detail, and auditable accounting pipeline mapping to the business bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers from non-EU jurisdictions into the French SARL and onward disbursements to suppliers or trading counterparties, triggering potential sanctions or unexplained wealth screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bilateral commercial contracts with counterparties, copies of all inbound wire instructions and purpose codes, outbound correspondence with supplier invoicing, customs import/export declarations (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens), Incoterms terms, due diligence on counterparty beneficial owners, and third-party sanctions screening certificate confirming neither the SARL nor counterparties are listed on OFAC/EU sanctions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the French SARL from shareholders may be executed through SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT for EUR transfers, using payment purpose codes that clearly indicate the nature of the flow (e.g., EU/IMF balance-of-payments categories such as 'equity capital', 'loans', or 'trade payments'). France does not impose exchange permission approval, but the SARL must retain evidence of the underlying contribution and report to Banque de France if yearly cross-border flows exceed the relevant threshold. A formal shareholder loan agreement, board resolution, and deposit proof must support the inbound credit, and the receiving bank must identify the ultimate source of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement from the French SARL should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR cross-border payments, SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated payments within the Single Euro Payments Area, and Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) for high-value, risk-mitigated transactions against presentation of invoices, bills of lading, and inspection certificates. For routine TikTok Shop retail operations, supplier and logistics payments may be consolidated using reputable multi-currency payout rails (e.g., Wise Business) in conjunction with the primary commercial bank account, provided that all transactions are mapped to underlying invoices and retained for local tax and transfer-pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign exchange forwards under ISDA / FBF master agreements
Market-standard deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/GBP forward contracts
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for balance-sheet hedging of acquisition or financing exposures
Currency options for protection in volatile e-commerce markets
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for exotic currencies lacking delivered fixing mechanisms, subject to French regulatory classification and bank acceptability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and general management report by shareholders (Ordinary General Meeting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate body; minutes recorded in Registre des procès-verbaux des délibérations des associés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the SARL's fiscal year end; for a calendar-year entity by 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine for a late internal meeting; any shareholder may petition the court to convene the meeting. Unapproved accounts cannot lawfully be filed and, if uncorrected, will trigger the RCS filing infringement procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) at the Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the shareholders' approval, and in any event no later than eight months after the fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice from the registrar; court-ordered filing under astreinte (coercive fine) commonly €500–€3,000 per month of delay; persistent failure is referred to the public prosecutor and may lead to court-ordered dissolution and RCS administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale) with supplementary schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities, filed by the second business day following 1 May of the year after the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing increases assessed corporate income tax by 10% after formal notice and triggers late-payment interest (0.20% per month); under-declaration may be sanctioned with penalties of 40–80% depending on good faith and regularity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner update filing (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) after any share transfer or shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS via Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the completion of any share transfer or any change in the identity or shareholding of beneficial owners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to €7,500 for the legal representative and €37,500 for the SARL; repeated or deliberate omission can support judicial strike-off proceedings and prohibition against managing certain companies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is compulsory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at fiscal year-end: balance sheet total > €4,000,000; turnover excluding VAT > €8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory where a parent company or group consolidation requires it, or in regulated retail/payment activities when the statutory auditor condition is triggered.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory financial statements must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC regulation 2016-06); EU-adopted IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts only. Annual accounts must be filed in electronic RCS format through GFC/Infogreffe.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must keep its own beneficial-owner register continuously up to date. No standalone annual UBO declaration exists in France; instead, after each share transfer or ownership change the company amends the shareholder/movement register and files an updated DBE with the Greffe du RCS within 30 days. The manager must present the updated ownership and UBO records at each annual general meeting to ensure they match the shareholders registered as of the fiscal year end.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (share transfer register)
Registre des procès-verbaux et des décisions des associés (minutes register)
Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (beneficial owner register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250–$900 per year for commercial domiciliation or registered-office service in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000–$15,000 per year when a statutory audit is required or voluntarily commissioned

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (for fiscal years opening on or after 1 January 2022); reduced 15% rate applies to the first €42,000 of taxable profit for SMEs meeting the strict statutory definition (turnover < €10 million and shareholding owned at least 75% by individuals).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% band on first €42,000; Research Tax Credit (CIR) 30% up to €100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) 20% up to €400,000; Young Innovative Company (JEI) exemption up to 30% of qualifying R&D wages; other territorial and urban regeneration credits (rare for e-commerce).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (perpetual carryforward under Article 209 CGI) but annually capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000; historical 5-year carryback (≤ €1,000,000) under Article 220 quinquies CGI has been repealed for fiscal years ending on or after 31 December 2025.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Liasse fiscale: Cerfa No. 2065-SD / 2065-IS plus annexes 2050 to 2058-A; mandatory electronic filing via the DGFiP web portal (professionnel.impots.gouv.fr) or EDI-TDFC for corporate return preparers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filed return, together with four mandatory quarterly corporate income tax prepayments (acomptes d'IS) due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; a final settlement (solde de liquidation) accompanies the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: filed no later than the second business day following 1 May of the next year. Fiscal year ending on any other date: filed within three months of the fiscal year-end. One-month extension can be obtained for state-aid thresholds but is rarely used for online retail SARLs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification of the SARL: SIREN, SIRET, French registered address, legal form, ISIN, APE/NAF code corresponding to ISIC 4791 (NAF 4791A and complementary 4791B if applicable), and name of the gérant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL must disclose its French domicile and full register data; non-resident shareholders/directors must provide identity data, date and place of birth, and complete foreign address, but no foreign tax ID is required on the 2065 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes BA / BB – Résultat net de l'exercice
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit (BA) or net accounting loss (BB) drawn from the statutory financial statements, including TikTok Shop commission revenues, live-stream sales margins, platform bonuses and foreign exchange differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All profit and loss of the French sales activity is aggregated in the French entity. Non-resident owners are not separately taxed on the SARL's accounting result; profit is taxed at SARL level before any distribution to foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expense items: fines, penalties, excessive director fees, non-deductible financing charges, non-deductible vehicle and entertainment expenses, 25% of car/light-vehicle depreciation if deductible only at 75%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, TikTok platform support fees and affiliate/agency commissions paid to related foreign parties must satisfy Article 238 A CGI formalities (actual activity, adequate counterpart, burden of proof on the SARL). Excessive payments to non-resident shareholders are re-integrated as constructive dividends and exposed to abuse-of-law recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions adjusting accounting profit to fiscal profit: exempt capital gains on qualifying patent transfers, investment tax credits, participation exemptions, and similar legal reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL is entitled only to deductions arising from its own French economic activity. Costs incurred for the private benefit of foreign affiliates are strictly disallowed and must be substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward tax losses used in the current fiscal year, subject to the €1,000,000 + 50% annual cap and supported by the 2058-A deficit schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax loss belongs to the SARL, not to the shareholders. Foreign owners have no right to step into or sell the loss position; losses cannot be attributed to foreign shareholders for their home-country reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box BF – Résultat fiscal imposable / IS brut
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable profit multiplied by 25% (or the 15% reduced band), generating the gross CIT before application of tax credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation for this item. The SARL's tax credits (family credit, foreign tax credits, CIR) are applied by the SARL and any refund surplus is payable to the SARL bank account, not to the shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic penalty of 10% of the net CIT due without prior demand; 40% if no return is filed within 30 days of a formal notice (mise en demeure); 80% if the administration discovers the omission during a tax audit. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month (2.4% per year). Missing or incomplete annexes trigger a fixed €150 penalty per schedule. Failure to e-file exposes the company to a specific fine of €150 per document.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under domestic law (Article 119 bis 2 CGI) on dividends paid by a French SARL to non-resident corporate shareholders. A reduced 0% rate applies to EU/EEA parent companies holding ≥ 5% of the distributable share capital for at least 2 years (Parent-Subsidiary Directive). For non-resident individuals, a 12.8% withholding applies under the flat-tax regime, plus French social levies where mandated. Treaty relief can reduce the rate (commonly 5% or 15%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty or PSD relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide the SARL, prior to payment: (i) an original or electronic tax residence certificate (TRC) confirming residence in the treaty/EU jurisdiction; (ii) a declaration of the beneficial ownership of the shares and holding period; (iii) documentation on the same form required by DGFiP (Form 5086 or equivalent); and (iv) for the PSD, evidence of at least 2-year holding. If full relief is applied at source, the payor must file a yearly withholding return (Form 2777-DIV) and retain the documents; if tax is withheld, refund claims are filed with the Direction des impôts des non-résidents (DRFIP) on Form 5000/5001 within the statutory claim period (generally 31 December of the second year following the year of payment).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: no statutory withholding tax on arm's-length interest paid to non-residents in a standard debt financing structure; the 75% withholding/surcharge regime applies to interest paid to non-cooperative states (ETNC); the Interest-Royalty Directive may exempt interest paid to related EU entities. Royalties and license fees for trademarks, know-how, software rights and live-commerce algorithms: domestic withholding of 33⅓% (Article 1678 bis CGI); reduced to 15% under the EU Interest-Royalties Directive where the beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the SARL (or the reverse) for at least 2 years; bilateral treaties often further reduce or exempt patent royalties but trademark/licensing royalties are rarely treaty-exempt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File are compulsory where the French entity's annual turnover or gross book assets exceed €400 million, or where it belongs to a tax-integrated group exceeding €400 million; a simplified transfer pricing documentation duty applies from €50 million (turnover or total balance sheet). In all cases, the French administration may request TP documentation below these thresholds if there is a serious presumption of profit shifting, particularly in digital/social-commerce flows.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies economic-substance principles through the general anti-abuse provision (abus de droit, Article L.64 LPF) and the MLI Principal Purpose Test. A French SARL used to stream TikTok Shop revenues must demonstrate real and credible French substance: local staff, offices, decision-making on stock/customers/marketing, and actual commercial risk. If characterised as a letterbox or conduit company, DGFiP may ignore the SARL, reallocate income to the foreign parent, deny treaty benefits, impose an 80% penalty and transfer the liability to the foreign beneficial owner. The SARL must therefore keep payroll records, lease contracts, board minutes and logistics documents showing operational control in France.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Under-reporting of Social Commerce Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or concealment of TikTok Shop sales, under-declaration of live-stream revenue in France, use of foreign shell payment accounts (Wise_B2B or similar) to mask French-source turnover, or false distinction between commission income and direct retail sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI: criminal fine up to €500,000 (increased to €2,000,000 and 7 years' imprisonment for aggravated fraud); in all cases, 80% penalty on the evaded tax plus 0.20% per month late interest, mandatory publication of the judgment, loss of good standing, non-deductibility of the fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant of the SARL faces personal criminal prosecution, civil restitution of the evaded taxes, travel restrictions (interdiction du territoire français), bank account freezing, surrender of passport, and disqualification from managing French companies. Article L.267 LPF allows the tax administration to collect corporate tax debts personally from the gérant where the gérant's intentional misconduct caused the non-payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Burden of Proof / Fake Substance (Shell Company)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL has no employees, no premises, no stock and no genuine commercial autonomy; all TikTok Shop purchase orders are routed through a foreign affiliate which collects the margin; the SARL merely passes commissions to a foreign parent; or the SARL licenses European market access to an offshore affiliate to shift profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article L.64 LPF abuse-of-law procedure: recharacterization of the transactions, reintegration of all shifted profits, application of the 80% penalty (when abus de droit is proven), suspension of statute-of-limitation periods, and additional withholding taxes on deemed dividends/royalties; in criminal cases the 80% penalty may be augmented by Article 1741 sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally subject to the full set of tax liabilities under Article L.266/L.267 LPF, criminal fines, imprisonment up to 5 years, prohibition from commercial activity, and travel bans. In insolvency proceedings, the gérant may be ordered to bear the company's tax deficit as part of the faute-de-gestion action.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Fraudulent Use of Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate use of TikTok Shop Payout or Wise_B2B to structure receipts into amounts below €10,000 to evade Sofico declaration, moving funds to FATF high-risk jurisdictions, or maintaining off-book wallets accessible to non-resident shareholders without accounting entry; assisting a foreign third party to launder sales proceeds through the French SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary and Financial Code: corporate fine up to €1,000,000 for money laundering; seizure of funds held in the payment accounts up to the amount of the illegal proceeds; automatic reporting to Tracfin; withdrawal of PSP access; publication of AML sanctions; and administrative penalties by the Auditeur de la conformité.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SARL are criminally liable for laundering, receiving up to 5 years' imprisonment and fines up to €375,000, plus civil restitution, freezing of personal assets, passport seizure and travel bans. The company's compliance officer (or the default gérant) may additionally face a management ban from the AMF/ACP.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distribution of dividends or payment of royalties/management fees to non-resident shareholders without applying the 25% (or 33⅓%) withholding, without obtaining a valid tax residence certificate, or using artificial interposed EU holding vehicles designed to circumvent the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payor (SARL) is required to pay the entire unreported withholding tax; the amount is increased by an 80% penalty for intentional non-collection and monthly late interest. The administration may attach the SARL's assets and payment rails, including TikTok Shop payouts, for the tax debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Article L.267 LPF: the gérant is personally liable for the unpaid withholding when it is proven that the gérant either collected or directed the payment without withholding tax and that the SARL cannot satisfy the claim. Criminal prosecution for fraud may lead to travel bans, civil recovery of the withheld amounts, and economic disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Accounting and Non-Intrusive Digital Filing Errors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false 2065/annexes, using a second set of books for TikTok Shop revenue, claiming fictitious inventories for live-sale products, intentionally underestimating closing stock, or failing to file the annual return for 3 consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% late filing penalty; 40% if relevant to a formal demand; 80% for fraudulent omission; late interest at 0.20% per month; €150 per missing annexe; criminal fine under Article 1743 CGI up to €500,000 with imprisonment up to 5 years if false accounting is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be held jointly and severally liable for the penalties and tax under the faute-de-gestion doctrine; a travel ban and prohibition on commercial management can be imposed; in case of insolvency, Article L.651-2 of the Commercial Code requires the gérant to repay the company's tax liabilities out of personal assets where gross negligence caused the shortfall.
